title: Gasdermin D-mediated delivery of caspase inhibitors to suppress pyroptosis.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Downloaded and opened all 12 Excel supplementary/source-data files. Supplementary Table 1 holds exactly 91 inhibitors (KGR-1..KGR-107, with gaps) x 8 human caspases = 728 rate constants, zero missing cells, sequences written as 3-letter residue names of length 4 or 5. The 10 source-data workbooks are figure-level curves (3-96 rows per sheet, mostly under 40). Files served openly from media.springernature.com, no login, licence CC BY-NC-ND 4.0.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: Units (M-1 s-1) come from the Supplementary Table 1 caption, not from a units column inside the sheet. Assay details (recombinant human caspases, kobs/[I] progress-curve fitting) and all mouse/cell-biology results were read in the article HTML, not re-derived.

a1_downloadable.note: Pass, verified. Every supplementary and source-data file downloaded directly from Springer's static host with no login. Article itself is CC BY-NC-ND open access despite Europe PMC flagging it closed.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: Pass, verified. The label is literally a column: one column per caspase (caspase-1, -3, -4, -6, -7, -8, -9, -10) holding the measured second-order inactivation rate constant kobs/[I] for each inhibitor.

a3_inputs_present.note: Borderline pass. Peptide sequences are present as text, but 53 distinct residue tokens appear and roughly 35 are non-natural (Tle, hGlu, Oic, Thr(Bzl), Phe(2-Cl), 2Nal, Cha, Dap(Cbz), Thz...). No SMILES (chemical structure strings) given, so each unusual residue would need a hand-built structure; protein language models cannot encode them.

a4_units_stated.note: Pass. Units M-1 s-1 stated in the table caption and consistent across all 8 columns. Values are stored as text with space thousand separators ('3 920 000'), so they need one cleaning step before use.

a5_enough_rows.note: FAIL, verified in the file. Only 91 unique inhibitors; 728 measurements in total across 8 caspases, i.e. 91 per caspase. The checklist needs ~1,500 labelled rows (or ~400 for classification). Even pooling all eight enzymes leaves fewer than half the required rows, over only 91 distinct molecules, so the effective sample size is 91.

a6_fits_laptop.working_set: ~1.9 MB of Excel files in total
a6_fits_laptop.note: Pass trivially; the whole dataset is a 28 KB spreadsheet.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Pass. Table contents match the text's description (tetrapeptide Ac-P4-P3-P2-P1(Asp)-AOMK inhibitors, caspase-1 selectivity of KGR-3, KGR-23, KGR-72); the paper gives no global compound count to contradict the 91 rows found.

a8_label_provenance.note: Pass. Labels are directly measured enzyme kinetic constants from progress-curve assays on recombinant human caspases, not another model's output and not computable from the peptide sequence.

existing_models.name: Partial-least-squares QSAR model for caspase-1 inhibitors (quantitative structure-activity relationship; reported in a 2025 natural-product virtual screening study, PMC13515187)
existing_models.score_and_split: R-squared 0.870 train / 0.838 test, 5-fold cross-validation Q-squared 0.814, on 185 caspase-1 inhibitors with pKi values; split appears random. Read from a web-search summary only, paper not retrieved in full.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Not established - I did not read the full paper.

existing_models.name: DeepCleave, a deep-learning predictor of caspase and matrix-metalloprotease cleavage sites (Bioinformatics 2020)
existing_models.score_and_split: Not retrieved; predicts cleavage sites in substrate proteins, which is a different task from inhibitor potency.

backbone.name: None suitable
backbone.hardware: CPU only would suffice, but no backbone fits: ESM-2 (a protein language model) cannot encode the ~35 non-natural residues, and ChemBERTa/MolFormer (molecule language models) need SMILES strings that the file does not provide.

integration.partner_dataset: MEROPS (peptidase and inhibitor database) or ChEMBL caspase bioactivities, joinable only after hand-building structures for every non-natural residue.
integration.join_key: No standard chemical identifier present - no SMILES, InChIKey or ChEMBL ID in the file; only in-house codes (KGR-n) and residue-name strings.
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Could not be written usefully at n=91: any pooled peptidyl-covalent-inhibitor selectivity model would be built mostly from other papers' data, making this file a small add-on rather than the dataset.

controls.positive_control: Available in principle: the model must recover the textbook result that Asp-Glu-Val-Asp (DEVD) is far better on caspase-3 than caspase-1, and Trp-Glu-His-Asp (WEHD) the reverse - both visible in the downloaded table.
controls.negative_control: Label shuffling would be runnable but meaningless at 91 compounds.
controls.external_validation: Mouse caspase-1 values exist in Extended Data Table 2 (not machine-readable), plus older Drag-lab tetrapeptide libraries; nothing joinable without manual curation.

honest_claim_h3: A model here could only claim: among 91 tetrapeptide/pentapeptide acyloxymethyl-ketone inhibitors designed by one laboratory around a fixed P1 aspartate, these sequence features track the measured inactivation rate for eight human caspases - a claim about one chemotype from one lab, not about caspase inhibitors generally.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use a short peptide inhibitor's amino acid sequence to predict how fast it switches off each of eight human caspase enzymes.
plain_idea.train_on: Each example is one covalent inhibitor written as four or five amino acid names (many of them laboratory-made, non-natural residues) with a fixed reactive warhead. There are 91 such inhibitors, verified by opening the file.
plain_idea.predict: The second-order inactivation rate constant (how quickly the inhibitor disables the enzyme, in units of inverse molar inverse second) for each of caspase-1, -3, -4, -6, -7, -8, -9 and -10, measured in test-tube assays with purified human enzymes - 728 measured values in all.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Chemists designing selective caspase blockers (for inflammatory disease) would want to know which residue at which position buys selectivity for caspase-1 over the apoptosis caspases; but with 91 molecules this is a medicinal-chemistry table to read, not a dataset to model.

more_or_better_data.why: The one quantitative model I found was fitted on 185 caspase-1 inhibitors; this paper supplies 91, i.e. roughly half as many, though it adds an eight-caspase selectivity panel that affinity-only sets lack.

confidence_score.why: The table reports a single rate constant per inhibitor-caspase pair with no replicates, standard errors or repeat measurements, so per-prediction uncertainty cannot be calibrated from it.

models_beatable.why: A partial-least-squares regression on 185 compounds with an apparently random split is the kind of model a modern approach beats, but with only 91 molecules here we could not demonstrate that credibly.

guaranteed_improvement.why: The existing model's weights are not available to run as a baseline, its compounds are ordinary small molecules rather than this paper's peptide chemotype, and the measured quantity differs (binding constant pKi versus covalent inactivation rate), so no condition for guaranteed improvement holds.

ml_idea: Considered and rejected: predict per-caspase covalent inactivation rate (kobs/[I]) from inhibitor peptide sequence, using the 8-caspase selectivity panel as a multi-task regression. Dies on sample size - 91 molecules, 728 measurements - and on the absence of machine-readable chemical structures for ~35 non-natural residues. The only salvageable version is a multi-paper pooling effort across a decade of HyCoSuL-style peptidyl-inhibitor libraries, in which this file is one small contribution, not the project.

effort.compute_note: Measured file sizes directly (28 KB main table, ~1.9 MB total). The 16 hours is an estimate dominated by hand-building chemical structures for ~35 non-natural residues and fixing the hyphen-inside-residue-name parsing (for example 'Phe(2-Cl)' splits wrongly on the hyphen separator); nothing was timed.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Open Supplementary Table 1 and count inhibitor rows. Done: 91 rows, 728 values - under the ~1,500-row bar, so the project is dead in ten minutes.

verdict_reason: Fails A5: only 91 inhibitors (728 kinetic values across 8 caspases), verified by opening the file.
